title: Order lookup returns every order for a crafted id
ticket: Pentest finding (high): GET /orders/' OR '1'='1 returns all orders in the database.

lines: def find_order(conn, order_id: str) -> Order | None:
cursor.execute(f"SELECT id, customer_id, total_cents FROM orders WHERE id = '{order_id}'")
return Order(*row) if row else None

output: AssertionError: query returned 4213877 rows for id "' OR '1'='1"

fixes: cursor.execute("SELECT id, customer_id, total_cents FROM orders WHERE id = %s", (order_id,))
cursor.execute(f"SELECT id, customer_id, total_cents FROM orders WHERE id = '{order_id.replace(chr(39), '')}'")
cursor.execute("SELECT id, customer_id, total_cents FROM orders WHERE id = '%s'" % order_id)
cursor.execute(f"SELECT id, customer_id, total_cents FROM orders WHERE id = '{order_id}' LIMIT 1")

explanation.cause: The id was pasted into the SQL text, so input could change the query itself.
explanation.why: A parameter is sent separately from the statement and can only ever be a value. Stripping quotes, %-formatting or adding LIMIT 1 all still build SQL from user input.

title: Any signed-in user can read any invoice
ticket: Bug bounty report: changing the number in /api/invoices/18231 shows other customers' invoices, names and addresses included.

lines: const invoice = await db.invoices.findOne({ id: req.params.id });

failing.test: invoices › a user can't read another user's invoice

fixes: const invoice = await db.invoices.findOne({ id: req.params.id, userId: req.session.userId });
const invoice = await db.invoices.findOne({ id: Number(req.params.id) });
const invoice = req.session ? await db.invoices.findOne({ id: req.params.id }) : null;
const invoice = await db.invoices.findOne({ id: req.params.id, deletedAt: null });

explanation.cause: The route checked that someone was signed in, not that the invoice was theirs.
explanation.why: Scoping the lookup to the session's user makes another user's invoice indistinguishable from one that doesn't exist (404, not 403, so ids can't be probed). requireSession was already enforcing the session check itself.

title: Log request bodies to debug the checkout errors
author: Sam Tan
description: We can't reproduce the 400s from the payment form. Logging every request body on /checkout for a week so we can see what clients send.

diff.text: export function requestLog(req: Request, _res: Response, next: NextFunction) {
log.info("request", { method: req.method, path: req.path, ip: req.ip });

explanation.cause: The checkout body holds card numbers, CVCs and addresses, and this writes them to the logs.
explanation.why: Logs are copied to many systems and kept for months: storing card data there is a PCI violation and a breach waiting to happen. Log validated field names and error codes, or a redacted copy, never the raw body.

title: Rate-limit failed logins per account and per IP
author: Lena Park
description: Credential stuffing attempts are up. This counts failed logins per username and per IP in a 15-minute window and refuses after 10, with the same message as a wrong password.

diff.text: export async function login(username: string, password: string, ip: string) {
if ((await failures.count(username, ip, WINDOW_15_MIN)) >= 10) throw new LoginError("bad_credentials");

explanation.cause: Nothing wrong: limits apply before the password check and the refusal looks like any wrong password.
explanation.why: Counting by username and IP slows both single-account guessing and spraying, and the identical error doesn't reveal which usernames exist or are locked.

title: Old password reset links work, fresh ones say expired
ticket: Support: customers clicking a reset link straight away get 'This link has expired'. One user says a link from an email in March still let them change their password today.

lines: export async function resetPassword(token: string, newPassword: string) {
const reset = await db.passwordResets.findOne({ tokenHash: sha256(token) });
if (!reset || reset.usedAt !== null) throw new ResetError("invalid_token");
if (reset.expiresAt > new Date()) throw new ResetError("expired_token");

failing.test: passwordReset › a token past expiresAt is refused

fixes: if (reset.expiresAt < new Date()) throw new ResetError("expired_token");

explanation.cause: The expiry comparison was inverted, so it refused links still in their window and accepted every link past it.
explanation.why: A reset link is a password in an inbox that may be read by someone else later; it must stop working after its window. Comparing against Date.now() keeps the same inverted test, and checking against createdAt or presence never looks at the clock at all.

title: Allow the partner dashboard to call the API
author: Priya Raman
description: The partner dashboard on its own domain gets CORS errors calling /api with the signed-in user's session. This lists the partner origin next to ours and keeps credentials on.

explanation.cause: The origin callback reflects whatever Origin the browser sends; ALLOWED_ORIGINS is declared but never consulted.
explanation.why: With credentials on, any website a signed-in user visits can call the API as them and read the responses. The callback should return the origin only when ALLOWED_ORIGINS.has(origin).

title: File download serves files from a sibling folder
ticket: Pentest finding (high): /files/ blocks ../etc/passwd as expected, but a name that climbs into /srv/app/uploads-archive is served. That folder holds exported payroll CSVs.

failing.test: files › a name resolving outside UPLOAD_ROOT is refused

explanation.cause: A plain string prefix check treats /srv/app/uploads-archive as inside /srv/app/uploads because the names share their first characters.
explanation.why: Containment has to end at a directory boundary, so the prefix must include the trailing separator. path.resolve already normalizes, so normalizing or resolving again changes nothing, and indexOf is looser still.

title: Remove a project's stored files when it is deleted
author: Marco Silva
description: Deleting a project left its uploads in the bucket forever. This deletes the project's storage prefix as part of the delete and records the action in the audit log.

diff.text: const project = await db.projects.findOne({ id: req.params.id });

explanation.cause: The files are deleted before the ownership check, so any signed-in user can wipe another project's uploads.
explanation.why: The request still gets a 404, which hides that the damage is done. Every side effect has to come after the authorization check, so the new line belongs below the ownerId test.

title: Verify signatures on the payments webhook
author: Ada Okafor
description: Anyone who found /webhooks/payments could post fake 'paid' events. The provider signs `${timestamp}.${rawBody}` with our shared secret. This checks the HMAC on the raw bytes and refuses timestamps older than 5 minutes. handle() already dedupes by event id.

explanation.cause: Nothing wrong: the HMAC covers the timestamp and the exact raw bytes, and the comparison is constant time.
explanation.why: Signing the raw body avoids JSON re-serialization mismatches, the length check keeps timingSafeEqual from throwing, and !(age <= 300) also rejects a missing or non-numeric timestamp, since NaN fails every comparison.
